title: Intelligent steering, failover, and prioritized load-shedding for multi-region routing
creator: Aisha Murthy
description:
Goal: Design and implement an adaptive multi-region request steering policy that combines latency-based routing, geo-pinning for session affinity, and capacity-aware steering with dynamic circuit breakers and prioritized load-shedding. 

Why: Current steering is static and either routes strictly by latency or by fixed geo preference. Under cross-region incidents or sudden traffic spikes we observed higher P99 latency and cascading failures when a hot region saturates. We need a single, auditable policy that: 1) maintains SLOs for latency and availability, 2) avoids saturating single regions, 3) supports session affinity for enterprise customers requiring geo pinning, and 4) gracefully sheds load by priority rather than full blackholing.

Scope: Proposal covers controller-side steering decision logic, region health scoring, per-customer pinning TTLs, capacity-aware weight adjustments, dynamic circuit breaker thresholds (percentile-based), and a prioritized load-shedding policy with configurable tiers (trial/free/paid/enterprise). Implementation touches the routing controller, config API, runtime fallback hooks, telemetry dashboards, and an ops runbook for emergency tuning.
acceptance_criteria:
1) Routing controller emits deterministic decisions for a mix of 10k synthetic requests spanning three regions and two customer tiers.
2) Under a simulated 40% capacity reduction in primary region, traffic rebalances such that global P95 latency stays within SLO bounds in 95% of trials.
3) Geo-pin settings honor per-customer TTLs and can be overridden by emergency policy with audit log entries.
4) Circuit breaker trip logic is driven by adaptive thresholds (e.g., 95th latency percentile vs historical baseline) and records metrics for when and why it tripped.
5) Load-shedding policy evicts lowest-priority requests first, with clear preserved capacity for enterprise tier.
6) End-to-end tests, dashboard panels, and runbook pages are merged and referenced in rollout plan.
work_log: 2026-02-24: Discovery session with PM and SRE. Mapped failure modes: region saturation, network partitions, config drift. Agreed on goals and customer tiers.

2026-03-02: Prototype health score model: health = weighted(sum(available_gpu_slots_normalized, inverse_p99_latency, recent_error_rate)). Weight tuning discussion: prioritize capacity and error_rate over raw latencies for failover triggers.
2026-03-04: Design review with infra and console teams. Feedback: expose pin TTLs in console and add audit log hook. Console team will own UI field; engineering to add API surface.

2026-03-07: Spike implemented for capacity-aware weights in staging controller (branch: feature/steering-capacity-aware). Synthetic load tests show reduced tail latency when steering uses capacity-normalized weights vs latency-only weights.
2026-03-10: Added dynamic breaker prototype: threshold = max(baseline_95pct * 1.4, historical_median + 3*stddev). Early telemetry looks reasonable but needs chaos testing under split-brain scenario.
2026-03-12: PM review: request addition of emergency override to pin enterprise customers to region for compliance incidents. Ops requested an on-call escalation playbook; added to runbook TODOs.
technical_notes:
- Region health score components: available capacity (slots), 95th latency vs baseline, error rate (5m window), and recent queue depth. Each input normalized and smoothed with EWMA(α=0.2).
- Steering algorithm: compute soft weights per region proportional to health_score * capacity_factor, then apply latency bias for nearby regions. Final decision respects geo-pin TTL unless emergency override enabled.
- Circuit breaker: percentile-driven with hysteresis and backoff. Open when 95th(latency)/baseline > threshold AND error_rate > X. Cooldown = geometric backoff; probe by sampling 1% of traffic to closed region.
- Load-shedding: token bucket per-region with priority queue. Requests tagged with customer_tier; admission checks allow enterprise>paid>free. Shedding policy configured via JSON policy in config service and feature-flagged for gradual rollout.
- Audit & observability: each steering decision emits tags {reason, health_components, weight_ratios, pin_status}. Dashboard panels required: per-region health, steering decisions histogram, breaker events, shed events by tier.
decision_log:
- 2026-02-26: Chose hybrid approach (capacity-aware + latency bias) over strict latency-only routing to avoid region overcommit. Approved by SRE lead (Leo Chen).
- 2026-03-04: Agreed to keep geo-pin TTL configurable per-customer; default 24h. PM objection to default longer than 7d due to compliance; compromise: default 24h with console override.
- 2026-03-11: Circuit breaker thresholds to be percentile-based rather than fixed ms; accepted to reduce manual tuning during model changes.
runbook_notes: Runbook draft at https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/RUN/Steering+Runbook. Includes emergency knob descriptions, how to pin/unpin customers, and suggested triage steps when a breaker opens frequently.
testing_plan: 1) Unit tests for health score math and alarm thresholds. 2) Integration tests with staging routing controller and runtime traffic generator (3 regions). 3) Chaos test: induce 30-60% capacity loss in primary region and verify redistribution. 4) Canary rollout by customer tier: enable for internal orgs, then low-risk paid customers, then gradual global rollout.
blockers: Need finalized console UI field for pin TTL (product dependency: PM-443)
KMS-based audit log schema must be approved before enabling override audit path (security review pending)
